name: Seneca Chamber arbitrary-call approval drain
summary: Chamber's public performOperations exposed an OPERATION_CALL action with attacker-controlled target and calldata. Because users had standing token allowances to their Chamber, an attacker could make the Chamber call token.transferFrom(victim, attacker, balance) and drain approved wallet assets.
notes: The EIP-1167 clone hard-coded the defect-bearing Chamber implementation at deployment and cannot be repointed.

The reported $6.4 million gross campaign loss covers repeated approval drains from Seneca users on Ethereum and Arbitrum. Approximately $5.3 million was later returned under a 20% bounty; recovery is separate from exploit-time gross loss.
The $6.4 million gross loss is a rounded reported cross-chain campaign total rather than a per-transfer incident-time valuation; later recovery is recorded separately.
